title: a to-write AT's note is write-once, and correcting it destroys the to-write state
body:
A `to-write` AT row's `note` can be set at creation and NEVER CORRECTED, and the only route to correcting it destroys the `to-write` state permanently.

DRIVEN, NOT REASONED, on an isolated estate against `3.0.0 (abe69906)`. `at new ST0001 AT-01.2 --covers AC-01.2 --note "..."` writes the note. Then:

- `at new` again refuses -- `a create must not replace it`. Its remedy is explicit that this is deliberate: "which keeps the note that a create would have eaten."
- `at edit` has no `--note` at all -- `error: unexpected argument '--note' found`. It re-cites `--file`, `--prose`, `--covers` and nothing else.
- No verb sets `to-write`. The surface is list / lint / green / red / na / new / edit.

So the note is writable once and never again while the row stays where it is.

THE PART THAT MAKES IT MORE THAN AN INCONVENIENCE: the only correction path is a state transition, and that transition is ONE-WAY. `data-model.md`'s Machine 5 records it in terms -- "`at new` enters at `to-write` and nothing returns a test to it ... `(any) -> to-write` is reachable through the typed API and through no command." So fixing a typo in the note of an unwritten test costs the `to-write` state, which cannot be restored, and `to-write` is the state that is lint-exempt for an absent citation. The correction is strictly more destructive than the defect.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG, MEASURED IN THE SAME RUN. On `red`, `green` and `n-a` the note IS correctable in place: a same-state re-assert succeeds at rc=0 and rewrites it (`at red` on a red row, `at green` on a green row, `at na` on an n/a row all return ok and the extract shows the new note). Self-loops are ratified at exit 0 in `data-model.md`, and `at.set` declares `from: &[]`, so this is the machine behaving as ratified. THE GAP IS ONE STATE WIDE, and it is the one state whose exit is irreversible.

RELATION TO 0090. Same family -- a field a create writes and no verb can rewrite -- but narrower and sharper. `0090` is a body with no writer at all; this is a note with a writer that is unreachable from the state it was written in. It is also NOT the `at edit --note` gap as first framed: adding `--note` to `at edit` would close it, but so would any verb that re-asserts `to-write`, and the second is the one the machine table already says is missing.

NOT FILED AS A BLOCKER. Nothing in the cut depends on correcting a to-write note, and the population is small. Filed because the remedy text on `at new` advertises note preservation as a feature, which is the thing most likely to stop the next person looking for the hole.

Found by vc, 2026-08-31, driving a question dc raised about whether `at edit` carrying no `--note` was a gap. dc's question was right and the first answer -- "correctable in place, not a gap" -- was right for three states of four.
